title: Electricity and wires (power-line stages)
summary: Explainers about electricity, voltage, circuits, power lines, birds or animals on wires, safety around electrical equipment.
world: a country road with a line of poles and wires (the hero) and, in front of it, one round grassy stage per idea, each with a short pole and wires

station_notes.line: the hero: the road, the poles and the live wires; always context
station_notes.feet: the bird's two feet on one wire
station_notes.path: the wire as an easy road for the current, the body as a hard one
station_notes.circuit: a loop that is open or closed
station_notes.bridge: a big bird touching two wires
station_notes.spacing: wingspan against the spacing of the wires
station_notes.pole: a pole where birds land, take off or perch in numbers
station_notes.fixes: covers, a longer crossarm, perch guards
station_notes.lineman: a lineman working on a live wire

power_on: current pulses run along the wire for a moment, so the viewer sees it is live
sway: the wire sways a little when something lands on it

show_levels: two wires take two colours: a violet one (higher voltage) and a teal one (lower)
push: pulses are pushed from the violet wire to the teal one through a gap between them

equal: two small rings light up at the bird's two feet in the same colour: same voltage
no_push: pulses run along the wire under the feet and none enters the bird

bypass: pulses flow along the wire, past the legs, instead of through the body
compare: a short thick road (wire) and a long thin one (body) are drawn side by side

open: a loop with a gap: the pulses stop at the gap
close: a second contact closes the loop and the pulses start to circulate

eagle_in: a big bird flies in and perches on the top wire
eagle_reach: the big bird spreads its wings toward the second wire
flash: a spark flashes where the wing touches the second wire, and the bird is thrown off

measure: a bracket measures the eagle's wingspan across the two wires
wires_apart: the wires move apart until the bracket can no longer reach both

land_pole: a large bird comes in to land on the crossarm of a pole, wires close together
flock: several birds land together, the line sags and sways until the wires touch

cover: insulating covers slide over the insulators and exposed parts
space_arm: the crossarm is extended so the wires are farther apart
perch_guard: a perch guard rises over the crossarm

bond: a lineman touches the wire with a bonding wand and takes the wire's colour
work: the lineman then works on the wire safely

subject.description: the small bird perched on the wire, or the big bird that is at risk

look_around: turns its head left and right, looking at what is being described
grip: its toes tighten around the wire
hop: a short hop along the wire
land: flies in and lands on the wire
take_off: flaps its wings and flies off

term_help: voltaje, diferencia, circuito, resistencia, envergadura, aislante, percha, potencial (copied from the narration; only terms that appear)
